name: task
doc:
The Zell-source part of task (see sema/stdsrc.rs for the rules).
Delay, Yield, All and Any are runtime functions (stdlib.rs), and so are
Channel<T> and Mutex (runtime/src/task_sync.c, through the rtChan*/
rtMutex* primitives); the rest is built from signals (rtSignal/rtWaker:
a pending Task<void> that rtFire completes once), per-object spin locks
(rtLock/rtUnlock on an int field, held only for a few statements, never
across an await) and the task context slot (rtGetCtx/rtSetCtx).

items.name: ErrCancelled
items.doc: ErrCancelled is returned by a cancelled wait that has a result (`Recv`, network I/O).
items.summary: ErrCancelled is returned by a cancelled wait that has a result (`Recv`, network I/O).

items.name: ErrPanic
items.doc: ErrPanic is in the chain of the error a panicked task yields to the awaiter of its `Task<T!>` (`errors.Is(err, task.ErrPanic)`); the error's message is `panic: ` plus the panic message.
items.summary: ErrPanic is in the chain of the error a panicked task yields to the awaiter of its `Task<T!>` (`errors.Is(err, task.ErrPanic)`); the error's message is `panic: ` plus the panic message.

items.name: All
items.doc: All waits for every task and returns their results as a tuple (`var (a, b) = await task.All(f(), g())`). With fallible tasks the result is fallible: the first error cancels the other tasks and is returned.
items.summary: All waits for every task and returns their results as a tuple (`var (a, b) = await task.All(f(), g())`).

examples.name: ExampleAll

items.name: Any
items.doc: Any returns the result of the first task to finish (all tasks have the same type) and cancels the others.
items.summary: Any returns the result of the first task to finish (all tasks have the same type) and cancels the others.

items.name: CheckCancelled
items.doc: CheckCancelled fails with ErrCancelled if the current task is cancelled.
items.summary: CheckCancelled fails with ErrCancelled if the current task is cancelled.

items.name: CurrentContext
items.doc: The context of the running task.
items.summary: The context of the running task.

items.name: Delay
items.doc: Delay returns a task that completes after ms milliseconds.
items.summary: Delay returns a task that completes after ms milliseconds.

items.name: Get
items.doc: Get is the value of k in the current context, nil if it is not set.
items.summary: Get is the value of k in the current context, nil if it is not set.

items.name: Go
items.doc:
Go is Spawn for functions without a result (`Spawn<void>` cannot
return the result of its task).
items.summary: Go is Spawn for functions without a result (`Spawn<void>` cannot return the result of its task).

items.name: IsCancelled
items.doc: IsCancelled reports whether the current task has been cancelled.
items.summary: IsCancelled reports whether the current task has been cancelled.

items.name: NewCancel
items.doc: NewCancel makes a cancellation scope under the current task.
items.summary: NewCancel makes a cancellation scope under the current task.

items.name: PanicMessage
items.doc: PanicMessage returns the message of the task panic in err's chain ("" if there is none).
items.summary: PanicMessage returns the message of the task panic in err's chain ("" if there is none).

items.name: PanicTrace
items.doc: PanicTrace returns the backtrace of the task panic in err's chain, one frame per line ("" if there is none).
items.summary: PanicTrace returns the backtrace of the task panic in err's chain, one frame per line ("" if there is none).

items.name: RunWith
items.signature: func RunWith<T>(c Context, f func() Task<T>) Task<T>
items.doc:
RunWith calls f in context c and returns its task; the caller's own
context is unchanged afterwards.
items.summary: RunWith calls f in context c and returns its task; the caller's own context is unchanged afterwards.

items.name: Spawn
items.signature: async func Spawn<T>(f func() Task<T>) T
items.doc:
Spawn runs f on a worker thread (not on the caller's stack, unlike a
direct call of an async function) and returns its task. f must have a
result; use Go for `func() Task<void>`.
items.summary: Spawn runs f on a worker thread (not on the caller's stack, unlike a direct call of an async function) and returns its task.

items.name: SpawnWith
items.signature: func SpawnWith<T>(c Context, f func() Task<T>) Task<T>
items.doc:
SpawnWith is Spawn with an explicit context (from CurrentContext or
NewCancel): its values and its cancellation apply to f.
items.summary: SpawnWith is Spawn with an explicit context (from CurrentContext or NewCancel): its values and its cancellation apply to f.

items.name: Timeout
items.signature: async func Timeout<T>(t Task<T>, ms int) bool
items.doc:
Timeout waits at most ms milliseconds for t. It yields true if t has
finished (its result is then available with `await t` at once), false
on timeout; t keeps running either way.
items.summary: Timeout waits at most ms milliseconds for t.

items.name: With
items.signature: func With<T, R>(k Key<T>, value T, f func() Task<R>) Task<R>
items.doc:
With runs f with k set to value; the value is visible in f, in what f
calls and in tasks started inside, and not after With returns.
items.summary: With runs f with k set to value; the value is visible in f, in what f calls and in tasks started inside, and not after With returns.

items.name: WithTimeout
items.signature: func WithTimeout<T>(ms int, f func() Task<T>) Task<T>
items.doc: WithTimeout runs f in a scope that is cancelled after ms milliseconds.
items.summary: WithTimeout runs f in a scope that is cancelled after ms milliseconds.

examples.name: ExampleWithTimeout

items.name: Yield
items.doc: Yield lets other ready tasks run before the current one continues.
items.summary: Yield lets other ready tasks run before the current one continues.

items.name: CancelHandle
items.doc:
CancelHandle cancels the code run in its Context (with RunWith or
SpawnWith) and every task started from it.
items.summary: CancelHandle cancels the code run in its Context (with RunWith or SpawnWith) and every task started from it.

members.name: Cancel
members.doc: Cancel cancels the context and every task started in it.
members.summary: Cancel cancels the context and every task started in it.

members.name: IsCancelled
members.doc: IsCancelled reports whether Cancel was called.
members.summary: IsCancelled reports whether Cancel was called.

items.name: Channel
items.doc:
Channel<T> is a FIFO channel between tasks. `task.Channel<int>(n)`
makes one with a buffer of n values (0: unbuffered, every Send waits for
its Recv). Copies of a Channel share it. `await ch.Send(v)` waits for
room, `await ch.Recv()` for a value and fails once the channel is closed
and drained; Send on a closed channel panics. `for v in ch` receives
until then (Next, the iteration protocol). The channel itself lives in
the runtime (ABI.md 10.7): waiting senders and receivers are queued
there and each is woken exactly once.
items.summary: Channel<T> is a FIFO channel between tasks.

members.name: New
members.doc: New makes a channel with a buffer of capacity values (0: unbuffered); the same as `task.Channel<T>(capacity)`.
members.summary: New makes a channel with a buffer of capacity values (0: unbuffered); the same as `task.Channel<T>(capacity)`.

members.name: Send
members.doc: Send waits for room (or a receiver) and sends v; it panics on a closed channel.
members.summary: Send waits for room (or a receiver) and sends v; it panics on a closed channel.

members.name: Recv
members.doc: Recv waits for a value; it fails once the channel is closed and drained.
members.summary: Recv waits for a value; it fails once the channel is closed and drained.

members.name: Next
members.doc:
The iteration protocol: `for v in ch` (inside an async function)
receives values until the channel is closed and drained.
members.summary: The iteration protocol: `for v in ch` (inside an async function) receives values until the channel is closed and drained.

members.name: Close
members.doc: Close closes the channel: pending and later receives drain the buffer, then fail.
members.summary: Close closes the channel: pending and later receives drain the buffer, then fail.

members.name: Len
members.doc: Number of buffered values.
members.summary: Number of buffered values.

members.name: Cap
members.doc: Cap returns the buffer capacity.
members.summary: Cap returns the buffer capacity.

members.name: IsClosed
members.doc: IsClosed reports whether Close was called.
members.summary: IsClosed reports whether Close was called.

examples.name: ExampleChannel

items.name: Context
items.doc:
Context is a snapshot of the context of a task: its values (an immutable
list of frames) and its cancellation scope. Pass it to RunWith/SpawnWith
to run code in it.
items.summary: Context is a snapshot of the context of a task: its values (an immutable list of frames) and its cancellation scope.

members.name: IsCancelled
members.doc: Whether the context's scope has been cancelled.
members.summary: Whether the context's scope has been cancelled.

items.name: Key
items.doc: Key<T> is a unique, typed key for a context value: `task.Key<Span>()`.
items.summary: Key<T> is a unique, typed key for a context value: `task.Key<Span>()`.

members.name: New
members.doc: New returns a fresh key (the same as `task.Key<T>()`).
members.summary: New returns a fresh key (the same as `task.Key<T>()`).

items.name: Mutex
items.doc:
Mutex is an async mutual-exclusion lock. The zero value is unlocked;
`await m.Lock()` waits until the caller owns it, `m.Unlock()` frees it
and wakes the oldest waiter, Go's sync.Mutex rules (DESIGN.md
"Асинхронность"): a running task may take it first, and a waiter that
waited more than 1 ms switches it to FIFO hand-off. Not re-entrant. The three words belong to
the runtime (ABI.md 10.6): the lock state and the queue of waiting
tasks; a Mutex is not copied while in use.
items.summary: Mutex is an async mutual-exclusion lock.

members.name: Lock
members.doc: Lock waits until the mutex is free and takes it (no starvation, no order).
members.summary: Lock waits until the mutex is free and takes it (no starvation, no order).

members.name: TryLock
members.doc: TryLock takes the mutex if it is free (and not in FIFO hand-off); reports whether it did.
members.summary: TryLock takes the mutex if it is free (and not in FIFO hand-off); reports whether it did.

members.name: Unlock
members.doc:
Unlock releases the mutex and wakes the oldest waiter (or hands it over
in FIFO hand-off); it panics if not locked.
members.summary: Unlock releases the mutex and wakes the oldest waiter (or hands it over in FIFO hand-off); it panics if not locked.

items.name: Task
items.doc:
Task<T> is the builtin type of a started async call: `await t` waits
for its result. This declaration only documents the methods every
Task<T> has; they are compiler intrinsics (sema/call.rs) and Task is not
a member of this namespace.
items.summary: Task<T> is the builtin type of a started async call: `await t` waits for its result.

members.name: Cancel
members.doc:
Cancel cancels the task and its descendants (DESIGN.md "Отмена"):
their waits wake with task.ErrCancelled and Delay returns at once;
`await t` then follows the usual rules for T! and T. Repeated calls
are no-ops and a completed task keeps its result.
members.summary: Cancel cancels the task and its descendants (DESIGN.md "Отмена"): their waits wake with task.ErrCancelled and Delay returns at once; `await t` then follows the usual rules for T! and T.

items.name: WaitGroup
items.doc:
WaitGroup waits for a number of tasks: Add(n) before starting them,
Done() when each finishes, `await wg.Wait()` until the count is zero.
items.summary: WaitGroup waits for a number of tasks: Add(n) before starting them, Done() when each finishes, `await wg.Wait()` until the count is zero.

members.name: Add
members.doc: Add adds n (may be negative) to the counter; it panics if the counter goes negative.
members.summary: Add adds n (may be negative) to the counter; it panics if the counter goes negative.

members.name: Done
members.doc: Done decrements the counter by one.
members.summary: Done decrements the counter by one.

members.name: Count
members.doc: Count returns the current counter.
members.summary: Count returns the current counter.

members.name: Wait
members.doc: Wait waits until the counter is zero.
members.summary: Wait waits until the counter is zero.
